neighbours.label: a family or companion noun after a possessive ('his sister', 'his wife'); the + pole takes office/role nouns ('his boss', 'lord protector')
fire: In 1799 the poet and his sister moved to a cottage in the hills.
The officer and his wife were both arrested for spying.
After the war the captain and his brother returned to Ohio.
The old farmer lived there with his daughter and two dogs.
Later that year the painter and her husband sailed for Italy.
The young king rode out with his cousin before dawn.
That summer the writer and his mother rented a house by the sea.
The doctor and her son opened a small clinic in town.
quiet: In 1799 the poet and his publisher moved to a cottage in the hills.
The officer and his driver were both arrested for spying.
After the war the captain and his crew returned to Ohio.
The old farmer lived there with his tractor and two dogs.
Later that year the painter and her agent sailed for Italy.
The young king rode out with his guards before dawn.
That summer the writer and his editor rented a house by the sea.
The doctor and her assistant opened a small clinic in town.
